title: Saline vs Silicone Implants: How to Choose
meta_description: Saline shows a rupture; silicone usually does not, so the FDA recommends scans. FDA ages: 18 for saline, 22 for silicone. A plain decision table.
excerpt: Saline and silicone share a silicone shell and differ in almost everything you would notice: feel, incision, age rules and what happens if one breaks. Here is a plain decision table, the FDA rules, and what gummy bear, teardrop, smooth and textured actually mean.
quick_answer:
Should I choose saline or silicone breast implants?

It comes down to feel, rupture and follow-up. ASPS says silicone gel feels a bit more like natural breast tissue; saline can go in through a smaller incision but may ripple more. The FDA approves saline from age 18 and silicone from 22, and recommends scans for silicone because its ruptures are usually silent.

images.alt: A comparison card titled Saline vs Silicone at a Glance. Saline: sterile salt water, FDA age 18 or older, uniform shape and firmness, deflates if it ruptures so you notice, no screening recommended. Silicone: silicone gel, FDA age 22 or older, feels a bit more like natural breast tissue, usually silent if it ruptures, first scan at 5 to 6 years, then every 2 to 3 years. What Happens When an Implant Ruptures
Saline
The shell leaks and the implant deflates, right away or over several days. The body absorbs the salt water.
Silicone
Usually no symptoms. The gel generally stays inside the scar tissue around the implant, so it usually takes a scan to find it.
Sources: FDA; ASPS.

sources.title: Types of Breast Implants
quotes: Saline-filled breast implants contain a silicone outer shell filled with a sterile saltwater (saline) solution. Some are pre-filled and others are filled during the implant operation.
Silicone gel-filled breast implants have a silicone outer shell that is filled with silicone gel.
The FDA approved saline-filled breast implants for breast augmentation in women age 18 or older
Silicone gel-filled breast implants are approved for breast augmentation in women age 22 or older and for breast reconstruction in women of any age.

sources.title: Risks and Complications of Breast Implants
quotes: You and/or your doctor will be able to tell if your saline-filled implant ruptures because the saline solution leaks into your body immediately or over several days and deflates the implant.
most silicone implant ruptures are without symptoms, known as "silent ruptures."

Occasionally when a silicone gel-filled implant ruptures, you may notice a decrease in breast size, change in breast implant shape, hard lumps over the implant or chest area, an uneven appearance of the breasts, pain or tenderness, tingling, swelling, numbness, burning, or changes in sensation.
Generally, when silicone gel-filled implants rupture, the silicone gel escapes through a tear or hole in the implant shell but remains confined within the scar tissue around the implant

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most effective method for detecting silent rupture of silicone gel-filled breast implants. An ultrasound is an acceptable alternative imaging for screening for rupture for asymptomatic patients.
The FDA has not detected any association between silicone gel-filled breast implants and connective tissue disease, breast cancer or reproductive problems.
Symptoms such as fatigue, memory loss, rash, "brain fog," and joint pain may be associated with breast implants.
These symptoms and what causes them are poorly understood.

sources.title: What types of breast implants are available?
quotes: The gel feels a bit more like natural breast tissue.
Saline breast implants provide a uniform shape, firmness and feel
Should the implant shell leak, a saline implant will collapse and the saline will be absorbed and naturally expelled by the body.
A leaking implant filled with silicone gel will not collapse.
Structured implants are filled with sterile salt water, and contain an inner structure which aims to make the implant feel more natural.
Form-stable implants are sometimes referred to as gummy bear breast implants because they maintain their shape even when the implant shell is broken.
The consistency of the silicone gel inside the implant is thicker than traditional silicone gel implants.
These implants are also firmer than traditional implants.
Shaped gummy bear breast implants have more projection at the bottom and are tapered towards the top.
If a shaped implant rotates, it may lead to an unusual appearance of the breast that requires a separate procedure to correct.
Placement of gummy bear implants requires a slightly longer incision in the skin.
Round breast implants have a tendency to make breasts appear fuller than form-stable implants.
Because round implants are the same shape all over, there is less concern about them rotating out of place.
Smooth breast implants are the softest feeling. They can move with the breast implant pocket, which may give more natural movement.
Smooth implants may have some palpable or visible rippling under the skin.
Textured breast implants develop scar tissue to stick to the implant, making them less likely to move around inside of the breast and become repositioned.
